evals.prompt: Triage the findings in v1.3.9.json (proftpd, built from tag v1.3.9 in ~/demo/proftpd, build root /home/me/demo/proftpd).
evals.expected_output: Runs tools/bundle.py --plan to count what selections would hold (112 merge keys, 13 checkers; a per-checker sample of 2 is 24), then asks once which findings (all, a per-checker sample, named keys) and which method and model per lane, for all four method lanes, including leaving a lane out. May bundle and run lanes.py assign first, since both are free, and put the counts per lane in the question. Starts no inference and no lane method before the answer.
assertions: Runs bundle.py with --plan before any bundles are read by a model
Puts the finding counts in the question
Asks for the method (and model) for Construction, Intent, Contract and Value or path rather than assuming one
Does not start inference or any lane method before the user answers

evals.prompt: Triage a per-checker sample of 2 from v1.3.9.json (proftpd tag v1.3.9, ~/demo/proftpd, build root /home/me/demo/proftpd). Inference with Sonnet; read every lane with Sonnet. Records only.
evals.expected_output: Does not ask: the selection and the plan are fixed. Writes run.json, bundles 24 findings from git at the tag, runs lanes.py assign (22 from the checker table, 2 NEGATIVE_RETURNS pending), runs inference on only those 2, runs one reader batch per lane (Intent and value or path), assembles triage.json with records.py, and reports counts per lane and verdict naming the triager (local subagents on Sonnet 5.5, nothing written to Connect).
assertions: Writes run.json before any lane method runs
Runs inference only on the findings lanes.py left pending
Each reader is given one lane's bundles and that lane's questions only
triage.json passes records.py validate
The report names who produced the verdicts, says how many lanes came from the table, and says nothing was written to Connect
The report states the sample size and does not quote a false-positive rate

evals.prompt: Triage these findings with Sonnet throughout: a MISRA_CAST on an implicit conversion, and a PARSE_ERROR saying an include file could not be opened.
evals.expected_output: The checker table places MISRA_CAST in Policy and PARSE_ERROR in Other, with no inference. Neither gets a reader. Each record sets only the two custom attributes (Defect Category Policy or Other, Triage Method None). The PARSE_ERROR is pointed at the coverity skill as a capture question. No override can give the Policy finding a method.
assertions: Runs no lane method for a Policy or Other finding
Does not argue with the MISRA rule
The records set only the two custom attributes
Names the PARSE_ERROR as a capture question for the coverity skill

evals.prompt: A reader returned 'false positive - global invariant' for a FORWARD_NULL with the reason 'callers never pass NULL' and no enforced_at. Assemble the records.
evals.expected_output: records.py assemble refuses (rule 30: no location, no dismissal) and writes nothing. The fix is the reader's: locate where the invariant is enforced (a caller audit is not a location unless the callers are all read and named), or return unresolved.
assertions: Does not invent an enforced_at to make the tool pass
Sends the finding back to the reader or records unresolved
Nothing is written on the refused run

evals.prompt: Plan: construction, intent and contract read by Opus, value-or-path executed with coverity-verify. Verify returned 'refuted by execution: line reached 412,118 times in 60 s, claim never false' on the harness route for one FORWARD_NULL and 'not a fuzz-triage candidate' for a RESOURCE_LEAK across a socket. Turn those into verdict files.
evals.expected_output: The FORWARD_NULL becomes 'false positive - global invariant': the claim that held is the invariant, the line and reach count under the budget are enforced_at, and it has a breaks_if; executed true; verify's route and its as_code/stubbed lists copied. The RESOURCE_LEAK becomes 'unresolved' with verify's tier as the reason. Both carry the method 'Execution: coverity-verify'; nothing falls back to reading.
assertions: Uses the mapping table in references/records.md
Marks executed true only for the execution method
Copies verify's route fields into the verdict
Does not re-read the RESOURCE_LEAK to give it a verdict under the execution method

evals.prompt: A producer handed over 12 candidates from its custom checkers, with a table file of rows for them (each row has a lane and the method Execution: coverity-verify), plus 3 ordinary CHECKED_RETURN findings. It expects value or path with coverity-verify. Inference with Sonnet; verify for value or path.
evals.expected_output: Runs lanes.py assign with the producer's table. The 12 candidates carry their checkers' own method, so they go to verify whatever lane they landed in, and none is off-lane. Before any verify run, it reports the 3 CHECKED_RETURN findings, which are in Contract with no own method, and asks per finding or per group: verify anyway, the contract lane's method, or leave untriaged. Records the answers as overrides with reasons in run.json.
assertions: Uses the producer's table file rather than inventing rows
Treats a row's own method as the method, not as off-lane
Runs records.py check-lanes (or equivalent) before any method
Lists every off-lane finding with its lane and reason, and offers all three choices
Each off-lane record carries method_reason

evals.prompt: Triage a per-checker sample of 1 from findings.json. The analyzed tree was a nightly tarball with no git history; I have the analyzed idir and the Coverity installation that wrote it. Read every lane with Sonnet.
evals.expected_output: Uses the idir as the source: bundle.py --idir <idir> --cov-bin <the installation named in <idir>/emit/version>, with a --tag label. Does not invent a git tag or read source from a working tree. If the idir is filed under another host, does not run reset-host-name on it: copies it first or asks. Asks the plan question before any lane method runs.
assertions: Picks --cov-bin from the version the idir records, not whatever is newest
Never runs reset-host-name on the user's idir
Never reads source from a working tree
index.json records source mode idir

evals.prompt: (Run non-interactively, as a scheduled task.) Triage a per-checker sample of 2 from v1.3.9.json, proftpd tag v1.3.9, ~/demo/proftpd, build root /home/me/demo/proftpd.
evals.expected_output: The selection is given, but the plan is not. Bundles the 24 findings and runs lanes.py assign, both free. Then it stops without choosing a model or a method. The report gives what is done (the bundles and lanes.json, with 22 lanes from the table), what is needed (counts per lane, the 2 findings left for inference, a method and model for each of the four method lanes, and the assigner's model), and the command that continues. It infers nothing from a TTY or the environment (rule 38).
assertions: Does not pick a model, a method or an execution route on its own
Leaves the bundles and lanes.json on disk
Reports the counts per lane and the plan still needed
Gives the command or answer that resumes the work

evals.prompt: Triage these 40 findings from our own CodeXM checker ORG_UNSAFE_FORMAT, which reports printf-family calls whose format is not a string literal. Read with Sonnet.
evals.expected_output: lanes.py assign marks ORG_UNSAFE_FORMAT unplaced. Proposes one row for the checker, not 40 per-finding decisions: from its description, it stands in for PRINTF_ARGS and FORMAT_STRING_INJECTION, so candidates Construction and value or path, with what decides between them. Shows the row and asks before writing it to a table file the user keeps. Then runs assign again with --table and continues.
assertions: Places the checker once, as a table row
Derives the row from the checker's description or the built-in it stands in for
Asks (or, unattended, reports and stops) before using the row
Writes the row to a table file the user keeps, not into the skill's own table
